---
name: mirage-tesseract
description: "."
applications:
  - id: tesseract
    role: primary
---

Mirage's Tesseract (CLI `tsrct`) edits layered `.tsrct` video and motion projects. It is not the
Tesseract OCR engine.

The pinned CLI release is [v0.3.1](https://github.com/mirage-hq/Tesseract/releases/tag/v0.3.1).
Mirage publishes motion, video, design and editor skills with schemas and authoring references:
https://github.com/mirage-hq/Tesseract/tree/v0.3.1/skills
Read the relevant upstream skill and its installation guide.

Install on demand into `$VOYAGER_HOME/tools/tesseract/0.3.1`.
Download the matching `tesseract-0.3.1-<platform>-<arch>.zip` and `.zip.sha256`;
verify before extracting. On macOS/Linux, pass that directory to the bundled
`install.sh`; invoke its `bin/tsrct` by absolute path. Windows `install.ps1`
accepts `-Prefix` (entry point `bin/tsrct.cmd`). No global install is needed.

Discover commands with `tsrct --help`, `project --help`, `export --help`, and
`project schema [--document]`. `project create` creates a portable `.tsrct`
archive containing one composition and packaged media/fonts. Edit via
`project checkout`/`commit` JSON or `project apply` action batches, not archive edits.
`preview` and `filmstrip` output PNG; `export` outputs H.264 MP4 or
`--format prores` ProRes 4444 MOV. Linux H.264 requires the documented external FFmpeg backend.

Telemetry is enabled by default: `tsrct telemetry disable` opts out;
`telemetry status` checks it. Mirage's [terms](https://github.com/mirage-hq/Tesseract/blob/v0.3.1/TERMS.md)
require a separate commercial-use agreement for for-profit businesses with
US$1M or more annual group revenue.
